name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT

  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 topic skills, and original article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below. Read that family's `SKILL.md`, then only the
   article references needed for the task. Nested skills are explicitly read by
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   article references. Do not load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Apply the guidance

- **Design:** connect each important choice to the user's task and target
  platform. Include necessary interaction states, adaptation, and accessibility.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Lists and tables Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Lists and tables organize rows into one or more columns, with optional groups, hierarchy, selection, insertion, deletion, and reordering. A navigation list can express an app's structure; a multicolumn table can compare attributes and support sorting. ## Best practices Use rows for text that people need to scan. Consider a collection for many images or highly variable item sizes. Support appropriate editing, including reorder even when addition and removal are unavailable. In iOS and iPadOS, table item selection for editing uses an edit mode. Distinguish selection feedback by purpose: keep a navigation row highlighted to show the current path; for a chosen option, brief row highlighting followed by a persistent checkmark may be more appropriate. ## Content Keep row wording short enough to avoid excessive wrapping or truncation. When items contain lengthy prose, show titles and reveal content in a detail view. Preserve recognizability at narrow widths; middle truncation can retain both ends of an identifying string. Give multicolumn tables descriptive noun or noun-phrase headings in title case without punctuation. If a single-column table has no heading, add context with a label or header. ## Style Choose grouping and row styles that fit the platform and data. iOS and iPadOS grouped lists use headers, footers, and spacing; watchOS elliptical lists visually roll content over a curved surface; macOS bordered tables can use alternating row backgrounds. Use row configurations appropriate to images, text, headers, and footers rather than rebuilding familiar arrangements unnecessarily. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS, visionOS An info/detail-disclosure button reveals additional information about a row; a disclosure indicator navigates into the row's hierarchy. Keep these meanings distinct. Avoid placing a section index beside trailing row controls because their targets can interfere with one another. ### macOS Support click-to-sort headings when useful, with another click reversing the sort. Allow column resizing. Alternate row backgrounds can help people track values across wide tables. Use an outline view when the data is hierarchical. ### tvOS Test nearby imagery against the focused row's expansion and rounded corners. Prepare images for those system effects and avoid adding a second corner mask. ### watchOS Favor shorter lists, but preserve access to the full expected dataset. Present relevant items first and offer more rather than silently dropping subscribed or owned items. Vertical page-based movement among row details works only with short detail views; a scrolling detail view prevents swiping directly between detail pages. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Collections](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/collections) [Outline views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/outline-views) [Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 21, 2023, June 5, 2023.

# Apple HIG: Inputs

Identify the device, primary input, and available accessibility alternatives. Read that input’s reference and its platform subsection before choosing gestures or control mappings. Preserve system-reserved behavior and familiar semantics; use custom interactions only where the task benefits, with discoverable alternatives and feedback. Test transitions between input methods as well as each method independently.

# Searching Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/searching) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Support finding content in the app, document, and system. Recents, predictions, completions, corrections, attribute filters, and scopes can reduce effort. Spotlight on iOS/iPadOS/macOS can expose indexed content without first opening the app. ## Best practices Give important search a prominent toolbar or dedicated tab position. Prefer one clear app-wide search, retaining local filtering when distinct sections justify it. Communicate scope with placeholder, title, or scope control. Offer useful suggestions before/during entry. Treat search history as potentially private and let people clear it. ## Systemwide search Index app content with descriptive metadata. Custom file formats need metadata import support for Spotlight. Contextual commands can initiate an advanced Spotlight query and show relevant filtered results. Prefer system Open/Save views for their built-in systemwide search, and supply Quick Look generation for custom document previews. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS; systemwide Spotlight support described here specifically applies to iOS/iPadOS/macOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Search fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/search-fields) #### Developer documentation — Core Spotlight #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 8, 2026, June 9, 2025.

# Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Feedback Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Feedback communicates state, outcomes, consequences, and recovery. Match delivery intensity to significance: passive status can remain available in context; unexpected irreversible loss needs attention before it happens. ## Best practices Make feedback accessible through complementary visual, text, sound, and haptic signals rather than relying on one sense. Put routine state near the relevant item. Reserve alerts for critical, ideally actionable information. Warn before unexpected irreversible data loss, while avoiding warnings for ordinary expected deletion. Confirm completion when the task is significant, such as a payment, rather than adding noise to every successful action. When a command cannot run, explain the reason and how to proceed. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### watchOS Avoid indeterminate wait indicators that imply people must keep watching. Reassure them when a notification will communicate completion instead. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Playing audio](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-audio) [Playing haptics](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-haptics) [Motion](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion) #### Developer documentation — UIKit #### Videos

# Undo and redo Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/undo-and-redo) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Undo/redo supports safe exploration when people can predict the affected action and see its outcome. ## Best practices Describe the target in menu labels or the iPhone shake confirmation. Reveal offscreen changes, for example scrolling to restored text, so people do not repeat undo because nothing seemed to happen. Avoid arbitrary history limits; support the meaningful action sequence since opening or saving. Group related incremental adjustments when a batch undo helps, and consider reverting a larger set. Use standard menus/shortcuts/gestures first; add dedicated buttons only when needed, with standard symbols in a toolbar. ## Platform considerations No additional visionOS rules are specified. Undo/redo is unsupported in tvOS and watchOS in this pattern guidance. ### iOS, iPadOS Preserve standard three-finger swipe and iPhone shake behavior. The system supplies Undo/Redo plus a trailing space in alert titles; add only one or two precise words describing the operation. ### macOS Put commands at the top of Edit and preserve Command-Z for Undo and Shift-Command-Z for Redo. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback) [Pointing devices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pointing-devices) [Standard keyboard shortcuts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards#Standard-keyboard-shortcuts) [Edit menu](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/the-menu-bar#Edit-menu) #### Developer documentation — Foundation #### Videos

# Keyboards Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Standard keyboard shortcuts](#Standard-keyboard-shortcuts) - [Custom keyboard shortcuts](#Custom-keyboard-shortcuts) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) Physical keyboards support text, navigation, and games on every platform except watchOS. Shortcuts normally combine a primary key and modifiers; game bindings often use one key. ## Best practices Support and test Full Keyboard Access on iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS. On iPad, use ordinary keyboard focus for content, text fields/views, sidebars, and suitable custom collections; let Full Keyboard Access provide access to buttons, segmented controls, switches, and all other controls. Preserve standard shortcuts; games should keep expected system actions such as quitting while allowing binding customization. ## Standard keyboard shortcuts Do not repurpose familiar combinations for unrelated actions. A standard shortcut may be reused only when its normal meaning has no place in the app, such as Command-I for Info when italics is unavailable. /bin/bash -lc "cat > result.md <<'EOF'
# Mac inventory table audit

## Basis and decisions

The target is macOS inventory comparison and row selection. "'`interface.md` is the sole interface evidence: it reports missing headers, inconsistent quantity alignment, no sort indication, selection immediately activating Delete, and an unexplained blank filtered result. “Verified” below means explicitly documented in that file, not reproduced in a running app.

Keep a flat multicolumn table. Separate selection from commands, make quantities comparable, expose the current ordering, and explain zero results without discarding the filter. This is a framework-agnostic specification; no Apple SDK is required.

## Ranked verified findings

Priority reflects likely consequence and task obstruction, not measured frequency.

| Rank | Observed problem and effect | Correction and basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Critical | Selecting a row activates Delete immediately. Merely choosing an item can initiate destructive work. Whether it actually removes data or opens a confirmation is unspecified. | Selection only updates selection state and feedback. Delete requires a separate explicit command, targets the selected stable record ID, and is disabled without an eligible selection. HIG distinguishes focus/selection feedback and recommends recovery for changes; separating these events is this audit’s concrete safety decision. See [Focus and selection — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#Best-practices), [Feedback — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback#Best-practices), and [Undo and redo](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/undo-and-redo). |
| 2 — High | Missing column headers obscure attribute meanings and units. | Give each column a descriptive title-case noun or noun phrase without punctuation. Proposed schema: Item, SKU, Quantity; confirm these fields against the real inventory schema. Show quantity units in a heading or nearby context if quantities are not all counts. This directly follows [Lists and tables — Content](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables#Content). |
| 3 — High | Inconsistent quantity alignment prevents comparison. | Right-align count values and their heading consistently; use a consistent numeric format. Store quantities as numbers, not display strings. If fractional quantities exist, align decimal positions with consistent precision appropriate to the unit. These are audit design decisions for comparability, not a numerical-alignment rule stated in the consulted HIG article. The table’s comparison purpose is supported by [Lists and tables](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables). |
| 4 — Medium | Sorting is indicated nowhere, so the ordering cannot be understood reliably. The description does not establish whether sorting currently works. | Provide sortable Item and Quantity headers; repeat activation reverses direction. Show a direction indicator on the active header plus an accessible ascending/descending description. Default to Item ascending. Click-to-sort and reversal follow [Lists and tables — macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables#macOS); the indicator and default are design decisions. Sort quantity numerically, with a deterministic ID tie-breaker. |
| 5 — Medium | An empty filtered list is an unexplained blank screen. People cannot distinguish no matches from failure or know how to recover. | Retain headers and filter controls; display “No items match your filters” with “Clear Filters.” Distinguish this from an inventory with no records, loading, and failure. Exact copy and recovery action are design decisions applying contextual state feedback from [Feedback — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback#Best-practices). Preserve clear filter scope per [Searching — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/searching#Best-practices). |

## Corrected interaction specification

Use single selection initially; multiple selection is not established as a requirement. Keep keyboard focus distinct from selected record identity. Use a full-row selection highlight and visible focus indication, retaining active/inactive context. Do not rely on color alone: expose selected state, column associations, header sort state, control names, and result count through the implementation’s accessibility mechanism. These are required implementation outcomes, not claims of accessibility testing. See [Focus and selection — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#Best-practices).

Allow column resizing, following [Lists and tables — macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables#macOS). Keep item identity recognizable at narrow widths. Alternating row backgrounds are optional HIG advice, not a verified defect or acceptance prerequisite here.

```text
state:
  records: map<stableID, InventoryRecord>
  filter: Filter
  sort: (Item, ascending)
  selectedID: ID or none
  focusTarget: control or row ID or none
  undoHistory, redoHistory

visibleRows = filterRecords(records, filter)
visibleRows = stableSort(visibleRows, typedComparator(sort), tieBreak=stableID)

on SelectRow(id):                 # click or table keyboard navigation
  require id is visible
  selectedID = id
  render selection feedback       # no command dispatch; no data mutation

on ActivateHeader(column):
  if sort.column == column: reverse sort.direction
  else: sort = (column, ascending)
  recompute visibleRows
  preserve selectedID             # identity, never a row index
  expose header'"'s current sort state

on ChangeFilter(newFilter):
  filter = newFilter
  recompute visibleRows
  if selectedID is not visible: selectedID = none
  # Keep focus in the filter when typing; do not jump to a row.

Delete.enabled = selectedID exists AND selectedID is visible AND record is deletable

on ExplicitDeleteCommand():
  require Delete.enabled
  targetID = selectedID
  if deletion cannot be restored:
    request explicit confirmation naming the target and irreversible consequence
    if cancelled: return without mutation
  delete targetID as one transaction
  if restorable: record inverse transaction; clear redo history
  selectedID = none              # never select another destructive target implicitly
  retain valid focus; if a keyboard-focused row vanished, use a nearby row
  announce updated result count and deletion outcome

on UndoDelete():
  restore exact record and ID; recompute using current filter and sort
  expose restoration outcome even if current filters hide the restored record
  # Do not silently clear filters to reveal it.

render:
  loading -> explicit loading state, not “no matches”
  failed -> explain failure with Retry; do not label it empty inventory
  records empty -> “No inventory items” and an appropriate Add action if supported
  records nonempty AND visibleRows empty -> no-match message and Clear Filters
  otherwise -> table rows
"'```

Restorable deletion should offer Edit > Undo Delete Item and Redo Delete Item, with Command-Z and Shift-Command-Z per [Undo and redo — macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/undo-and-redo#macOS). Do not require confirmation for every ordinary undoable deletion. Warn before unexpected irreversible loss per the Feedback guidance. Persistence and deletion reversibility must be determined before implementation.

Headers, filter controls, Clear Filters, and Delete must be keyboard reachable using the host’s conventions; arrows within the table select rows without executing Delete. Preserve standard keyboard commands and test Full Keyboard Access as advised by [Keyboards — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards#Best-practices). These interaction mappings are specified behavior, not executed observations.

## Worked before/after

The following records are invented test fixtures, not supplied inventory data: A = Bolts, quantity 2; B = Nuts, quantity 10; C = Washers, quantity 3.

**Before, as described:** values lack headings and quantity alignment varies; ordering is unexplained. Selecting B activates Delete. Applying a filter with no matches leaves a blank screen. The actual row order and deletion outcome are unknown.

**After:** the initial Item ascending view has descriptive headings and aligned counts:

```text
Item ↑       SKU    Quantity
Bolts        A             2
Nuts         B            10
Washers      C             3
```

Select B: Nuts is highlighted; all three records remain; Delete becomes available. Activate Quantity: ascending order is A (2), C (3), B (10), with Quantity’s ascending indicator. B stays selected by ID. Activate Quantity again: B (10), C (3), A (2), with descending indication. Only a separate Delete command can remove B; an undoable implementation offers Undo Delete Item, which restores B with quantity 10 under the current ordering.

Apply an Item filter of “Cable”: show “No items match your filters,” a zero result count, and Clear Filters. Clear the hidden selection and disable Delete. Clear Filters restores the rows with the current sort preserved, without restoring a hidden destructive target automatically.

## Acceptance checks

These are pending checks for a future implementation, not passing runtime test results.

1. Every data column has a descriptive heading; quantities use a consistent alignment and unit/precision policy. Resizing leaves item identities understandable.
2. Clicking or keyboard-selecting B changes selection only: record count, data, and deletion history stay unchanged. No deletion confirmation opens merely from selection.
3. With no selection, Delete is disabled and command dispatch cannot delete. With B selected, only explicit Delete affects B. Cancelled irreversible deletion changes nothing; successful restorable deletion can be undone exactly and redone.
4. With fixture quantities 2, 10, 3, Quantity ascending yields 2, 3, 10 and descending yields 10, 3, 2. Repeated header activation reverses direction. Equal values have deterministic order. Visual and accessible sort states agree with actual ordering.
5. Sorting preserves B’s selection by ID. Filtering B out clears selection and disables Delete; clearing filters does not select a replacement automatically.
6. Zero filtered results retain the filter, show the no-match explanation and working Clear Filters, and preserve the current sort. Truly empty, loading, and failed states have distinct messages and appropriate recovery.
7. Keyboard-only and Full Keyboard Access checks reach all actions; focus and selection remain perceivable. Accessibility inspection confirms header/cell relationships, named controls, selected state, sort direction, result count, and useful outcome feedback. Check active/inactive selection and narrow layouts on the actual Mac implementation.

## Evidence limits and guidance trace

No source code, screenshot, runtime, actual inventory schema, persistence model, SDK, device, GUI, or accessibility execution was supplied or performed. Alignment, contrast, target sizes, localization, rendering, numeric accuracy, actual deletion, and assistive-technology behavior cannot be independently verified. The five findings are verified only against the written interface description. Corrected behavior and examples are specifications, not a patched application.

Read the installed root `.agents/skills/apple-hig/SKILL.md` first. Routed through layout-and-organization’s `SKILL.md` to `references/lists-and-tables.md`; consulted the root topic index for the exact table and selection topics. Also read the patterns and inputs family `SKILL.md` files before their selected articles: Searching, Feedback, Undo and redo, Focus and selection, and Keyboards. Each file was consumed with a separate single-file shell command. The selected families route directly to these article references; they did not prescribe an intervening topic procedure.

All guidance came from those installed local references (dated 2026-10-25 snapshot/retrieval metadata). Official links above provide attribution only; no web pages or videos were opened, and no newer guidance or API availability was verified. Source-backed guidance is distinguished from audit-specific design decisions throughout.
